questions.topic: The exposition of a fugue and its order of entries
questions.learningObjective: Identify the first entry in a fugue exposition
questions.stem: On the night of March 12 my log notes the soprano voice states the subject first in a three-voice fugue.

options.text: The exposition begins with the subject in the highest voice.

questions.explanation: A fugue exposition opens with the subject stated by one voice. The answer and countersubject follow in later entries, not at the start.
questions.hint: The first voice sings the subject itself.

options.text: Four, three, two, one.
Two, one, three, four.
Three, one, two, four.
One, two, three, four.

questions.explanation: Tonic closest, then dominant, subtonic, supertonic. Key distance governs the rank.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What constrains a countersubject
questions.stem: On July 28 my log asks whether a countersubject must avoid parallel fifths with the subject.

options.text: No, parallel fifths are allowed freely.
Yes, parallel fifths are avoided.
Yes, but only in minor keys.
No, only if it is invertible.

questions.explanation: Good counterpoint avoids parallel fifths between the countersubject and subject. Key and invertibility do not override that.

questions.topic: How much countersubject an exposition needs
questions.stem: My August 28 log counts one countersubject in a four-voice exposition.
questions.explanation: One countersubject appears in this log. The count need not match the voice count.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Computing the measure of the last entry
questions.stem: On September 28 I computed the last entry measure for a twelve-measure subject in five voices.

answer.exemplar: With twelve-measure subjects, the fifth voice enters at measure forty-nine, after four twelve-measure staggered entries plus one measure of overlap.

questions.explanation: Staggered entries begin every twelve measures. The fifth voice enters after four prior starts, accounting for overlap.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Reading a canon's entries and spotting the stretto

stimulus.body: Entry BB begins at measure one. Entry CC begins at measure four. Entry DD begins at measure five. The subject lasts three measures.

questions.stem: My October 28 log asks which pair forms a stretto.

options.text: BB and CC, because CC enters at the end.
options.misconception: entry at boundary is not overlap

options.text: BB and DD, because they are four measures apart.
CC and DD, because DD enters before CC finishes.
None, because BB and CC do not overlap.

questions.explanation: DD enters at measure five, before CC's three-measure subject ends at measure six. That overlap is a stretto.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The exposition of a fugue and its order of entries
questions.stem: On November 28 my log notes the first entry in a fugue in B-flat major.

options.text: A free episode in the tonic.
The answer in the dominant.
The countersubject in the tonic.
The subject in the tonic.

questions.explanation: The exposition opens with the subject in the tonic. Answer, countersubject, and episodes follow.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Comparing a fugue's subject with its answer
questions.stem: On January 28 I compared the subject and answer to find the transposition interval.

answer.exemplar: The answer transposes the subject down a fourth to the dominant, preserving the melodic contour and every interval.

questions.explanation: The transposition is a fourth down. Keeping contour and intervals defines the answer.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Reading a canon's entries and spotting the stretto

stimulus.body: Entry EE begins at measure one. Entry FF begins at measure two. Entry GG begins at measure eight. The subject lasts five measures.

questions.stem: My February 28 log asks which pair forms a stretto.

options.text: EE and GG, because they are seven measures apart.
FF and GG, because they are six measures apart.
EE and FF, because FF enters before EE finishes.
None, because EE and FF are adjacent.

questions.explanation: FF enters at measure two, before EE's five-measure subject ends at measure five. That overlap is a stretto.
